facts.text: Lynyrd Skynyrd wrote Sweet Home Alabama as a response to Neil Young's Southern Man and Alabama.
The song became the band's biggest hit, reaching number eight on the Billboard Hot 100.
Guitarist Ed King wrote the song's opening guitar riff.
Paranoid was written quickly as a last-minute addition to Black Sabbath's second album.
The record company changed the album title from War Pigs to Paranoid.
Paranoid became Black Sabbath's only top-five UK single.
Holy Diver was the title track of Dio's 1983 debut album after leaving Black Sabbath.
The music video was filmed at the burned-out St Mark's Church in east London.
Ronnie James Dio formed the band Dio with former Rainbow drummer Vinny Appice.
Country guitarist and producer Chet Atkins produced Jerry Reed's Amos Moses.
Amos Moses reached number eight on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1970.
Jerry Reed was also known for his guitar playing and songwriting.
MTV edited the Symphony of Destruction video because of its assassination scene.
The song was released as a single from Megadeth's Countdown to Extinction album.
Dave Mustaine wrote the song with bassist David Ellefson.
Master of Puppets was recorded at Sweet Silence Studios in Copenhagen.
The song is the title track of Metallica's 1986 album Master of Puppets.
Cliff Burton and Kirk Hammett included a homage to David Bowie's Andy Warhol in the recording.
Accounts differ over whether Chop Suey! was originally called Suicide or Self-Righteous Suicide.
The song was released as the first single from Toxicity.
Chop Suey! was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance.
Stayin’ Alive was written and recorded for the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack.
The recording uses a two-bar loop from the Bee Gees song Night Fever.
Stayin’ Alive spent four weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100.
Ozzy Osbourne sings the chorus with Zakk Wylde on Stillborn.
Stillborn was released on Black Label Society's album The Blessed Hellride.
Zakk Wylde founded Black Label Society in 1998.
Tribute was Jack Black and Kyle Gass's first live song as Tenacious D.
The single reached number two on the UK Singles Chart.
Tenacious D began as a comedy rock duo formed by Jack Black and Kyle Gass.
Filming Sleep Now in the Fire caused the New York Stock Exchange doors to close.
Michael Moore directed the music video.
The song appears on Rage Against the Machine's album The Battle of Los Angeles.
The limited Du riechst so gut '98 edition came in a scented digipak.
Du riechst so gut was Rammstein's first single.
The 1998 version was released with a second music video.
Hips Don’t Lie reworked Wyclef Jean's song Dance Like This.
Wyclef Jean appears on the recording.
The song became Shakira's first number-one single in the United States.
Belchior wrote Como Nossos Pais, which Elis Regina recorded.
The recording appeared on Elis Regina's 1976 album Falso Brilhante.
Elis Regina was a Brazilian singer known by the nickname Pimentinha.

scenarios.title: Eu Nasci Há Dez Mil Anos Atrás

facts.text: Eu Nasci Há Dez Mil Anos Atrás is the title track of Raul Seixas's 1976 album.
The album was Raul Seixas's last with Paulo Coelho as songwriting partner before their 1978 reunion.
Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian writer who collaborated with Raul Seixas on songs.
Johnny Cash performed Cocaine Blues at Folsom State Prison in January 1968.
The performance appears on the live album At Folsom Prison.
Folsom Prison Blues was one of Cash's earlier prison-themed songs.
